title: Public cross-hand opponent-context feasibility
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A compact outcome-independent public action context accumulated across hands can identify the six heterogeneous broad-league opponent styles on fresh sessions (at least 50% accuracy by 32 hands and 75% by 64, with every class at least 50%), supporting a context-conditioned learned policy that can specialize without benchmark-specific rules.
material_change: Generate deterministic 64-hand sessions with frozen Standard10 hero against six training and three SHA-disjoint holdout policies. Build only public street-by-action rates and activity counts, fit horizon-specific linear classifiers on eight sessions per training policy, evaluate on four untouched sessions per policy and unseen holdout sessions, and save raw decks/actions. No Slumbot and no policy-strength claim.
baseline: Existing shared residual gradients conflict across opponent-seat groups, while MGDA/CAGrad and direct-greedy ES did not yield scalable directions. Current policies observe only within-hand history and cannot carry opponent evidence across hands.
notes: The 3,072 training hands are environment hands used only to form session-level representation examples; no policy weights were trained and no Slumbot hands were used.

The aggregate 64-hand accuracy gate passed, but the preregistered minimum-class breadth gate failed (25% versus 50%). Unseen-policy entropy near zero reveals severe OOD overconfidence. This rejects only the raw unregularized classifier, not cross-hand context universally.

result.summary: Frozen Standard10 generated 84 deterministic 64-hand public-only sessions across six training and three SHA-disjoint holdout policies. The linear classifier reached 62.5% at 32 hands and 79.17% at 64 hands on untouched training-policy sessions, but minimum per-class accuracy was only 25% and unseen holdout predictions were pathologically overconfident.
result.conclusion: Public cross-hand action counts contain aggregate opponent-style signal, but the current unregularized linear readout fails breadth and OOD calibration. It is unsafe to condition a learned poker policy on this representation as implemented. The result is a mechanism-level rejection of the raw readout, not evidence that cross-hand adaptation is intrinsically unlearnable or undertraining evidence about a policy.
result.next_step: Reuse the frozen session-feature evidence in a zero-new-hand nested-CV L2 and temperature-calibration control; keep the existing untouched test sessions sealed until model selection is complete.
